title: 27.2 A Voltage-Biased CMOS Hall Sensor with 1.0sµT(3σ) Offset and a 60nT/√Hz Noise-Floor
problem: Traditional current-biased Hall sensors exhibit large offset errors (tens of µT), limiting their use in precision applications like compasses and current sensors; voltage-biased architectures may offer lower offset but require novel readout design.
motivation: Precision magnetic field measurement (DC magnetic sensing) in CMOS is hindered by large offsets; reducing offset by 3x over prior art enables wider adoption in wearables and embedded systems.
method: The sensor uses voltage-biasing (applying a fixed voltage across the sensor rather than driving current through it) instead of the traditional current-biased approach, with a circuit designed to minimize measurement errors. Two sensing elements output their signals as currents rather than voltages, which allows them to be easily subtracted from each other to cancel fixed systematic errors (offset) and reduce noise. The design is built in standard 0.18-micrometer CMOS technology.
key_novelty: This voltage-biased architecture achieves 3 times lower offset error (1.0 microTesla) and 5 times lower noise (60 nanoTesla per root-hertz) than current-biased sensors, demonstrating that this architectural change substantially improves precision magnetic field measurement.
contributions: Voltage-biased Hall sensor topology reducing offset through dual-arrangement current output
Low-offset readout circuit achieving 1.0µT (3σ) offset in 0.18µm CMOS
Improved noise floor to 60 nT/√Hz (5x reduction vs prior work)
3x offset improvement compared to state-of-the-art current-biased sensors

metrics.other: 3x offset reduction, 5x noise improvement vs prior art

limitations: Power consumption, temperature range, and linearity not discussed; application-specific performance (compass accuracy, current sensing range) not detailed.
